name: Dumbbell Single-Leg Calf Raise
equipmentItems: Support post or wall for balance
grip: Working side hand holds dumbbell at side with straight arm; non-working side hand touches post for balance.
description: Perform unilateral ankle plantar flexion on a raised calf block while holding a dumbbell on the working side, isolating the gastrocnemius under loaded stretch.
setup: Stand on a raised calf block or sturdy platform with the ball of the working foot on the edge and the heel hanging freely.
Hold a dumbbell at your side on the working side with arm extended.
Hook the non-working foot behind the working ankle and place your free hand lightly against an upright post or wall for balance.
instructions: Lower your working heel smoothly below the platform level into deep ankle dorsiflexion until you feel a complete stretch through the calf.
Press forcefully through the ball of the foot into full plantar flexion, rising onto your tiptoes as high as possible.
Hold the peak contraction at the top for a moment, squeezing the calf muscle.
Lower slowly under complete control back into the full bottom stretch before beginning the next repetition.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the opposite leg.
cues: Press straight up through the ball of the foot.
Keep the working knee motionless and softly unlocked.
Use the support post only for balance, not for assistance.
commonMistakes: Bending the working knee into a single-leg squat to assist the lift.
Cutting the bottom stretch short without letting the heel drop below the block.
Pushing off the wall or post with the free hand.

logging.example: Single 18 kg dumbbell held on working side: record 18 kg.
logging.note: Record the mass of the single dumbbell used. If performed with bodyweight only, record 0 kg external load.

variantNote: Unilateral standing calf raise on a raised platform holding a single dumbbell on the working side with knee straight to isolate gastrocnemius.
reviewNotes: Drafted from FitTrack ID 72 (Dumbbell Single-Leg Calf Raise).
Requires strict unilateral depiction: working foot on block with heel in full dorsiflexion/plantar flexion, opposite foot hooked behind ankle.
